To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) when the input variables are measured on more than an ordinal scale, a stable weak order can be produced, and (2) when the input variable are measured on an ordinal scale, partial orders are possible, but a stable weak order is not possible.

(1) information from ordinal scale measures cannot be integrated to produce a stable output, (2) a partial order can be obtained, (3) the partial order is affected by the number and nature or the input variables and their relationships, and (4) a partial order is not affected by the number of levels of each input variable.

When information is combined from several ordinal variables, the output variable is partially ordered and the amount of order depends on the number of input variables, the relationship between them, and trade-offs between them."
In summary, our research is concerned with
the integration of information from ordinal scale input variables.
how to combine information from several ordinal scale variables to produce a stable output variable.
the integration of information from ordinal scale input variables and the implications for psychological processes and theories that use ordinal scale variables.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the measurement level of the input variables is an important consideration in the development of psychological models of integration.
the level of information contained in a set of variables can be increased by increasing the level of measurement.
the integration of information from ordinal variables produces a partial ordering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the level of scale measurement of input variables has a major impact on the kind of model that can be developed for psychological processes.
the level of information in a variable is determined by the number and nature and relationship between the dimensions of the variable, not by the level of measurement.
the kind of psychological models we apply to data depends on the measurement scales of the input variables, which is an issue that has received insufficient attention.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the level-of-measurement issue is not a technicality that can be ignored.
the measurement level of input variables affects the nature of the output variable.
the level at which the input variables are measured affects the nature of the output.
